newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIAN CHEMICAL PLANT STABILISES FINANCES.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIAN CHEMICAL PLANT STABILISES FINANCES.

text.p: Bulgaria's chemical fertiliser producer Chimko, which is offered for partial privatisation, said on Friday it was stabilising its financial state and projected revenue from sales of $161.6 million in 1997.
The plant's spokeswoman Silvia Nakova said the revenue figure included $128 million from export sales.
"The constant trend in stabilising Chimko's finances continues," Nakova told Reuters.

Bulgaria plans to offer for sale a 60 percent stake in Chimko and the plant's 1997 business plan, adopted by the directors board on Thursday, envisages to finalise the deal within the first half of the year.
The plant, which imports 64 percent of its raw materials and exports 92 percent of its products, had a pre-tax revenue of 8.4 billion levs for the first 11 months of the year, Nakova said.
She said that from January until December the plant had produced some 717,000 tonnes of carbamide, 484,000 tonnes of ammonia, 12,000 tonnes of carbon sulphide and more than 2,500 metres of argon.
The Vratsa-based plant plans to produce next year 785,000 tonnes of carbamide, 525,000 tonnes of ammonia, 17,000 tonnes of carbon sulphide and 2.6 million metres of argon.
Chimko has 20 installations, including for reforming, carbamide, carbon sulphide, carbon dioxide and a catalytic installation.

Earlier this year the plant set up a joint venture with Frankfurt-based Messer Grieshelm GmbH, a subsidiary of Germany's Hoechst , to distribute industrial gases in the region. HIMKO has 49 percent and the Germans have the remaining stake.
